documents.unit: Office of the Provost, Center for Teaching Excellence
documents.title: Generative AI and Pedagogy at SMU
documents.summary: The Center for Teaching Excellence page says using AI is at the faculty member's discretion, requires every syllabus to address AI, and adds privacy and output-validation rules for all community members. It also contains a Q&A with advice on assignment design, detection and faculty use of AI.
documents.stance_why: The page states "It is at the discretion of the faculty member whether to use Generative AI in their classroom" and requires only that faculty "communicate to students about the use of AI via their syllabus", so it sets no stance itself and delegates to instructors.

units.why: The page says "It is at the discretion of the faculty member whether to use Generative AI", so the university sets no rule and hands the decision to instructors; P04 fits because the choice is per instructor.
units.anchor: It is at the discretion of the faculty member whether to use Generative AI in

units.why: "SMU requires that faculty communicate to students about the use of AI via their syllabus" is a binding duty on instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus, which is P09.
units.anchor: SMU requires that faculty communicate to students about the use of AI via their syllabus
units.fit_note: The same sentence adds that SMU provides a statement builder tool to help faculty write the statement.

units.why: "Faculty who use AI in the classroom should provide clear guidelines" for graded, ungraded and self-study work is a recommendation on how fully the expectations should be stated; it is the syllabus or assignment-instruction duty, P09, with modality should.
units.anchor: should provide clear guidelines around AI use in the class for graded and ungraded assignments
units.fit_note: It also names the scope of the guidelines: graded and ungraded work, self-study and other SMU support.

units.why: The same sentence asks for "a disclosure statement if AI is used for other pedagogical aspects such as assignment building or grading", which is instructors telling students about their own AI use (P47), not the student-disclosure types.
units.anchor: a disclosure statement if AI is used for other pedagogical aspects such as assignment building

units.why: "having access to data does not imply permission to scrape the data or use it to train an AI model" limits what faculty may do with data in AI tools; P50 is nearest but this is about permission to use data, not protecting personal data.
units.anchor: having access to data does not imply permission to scrape the data or use it
units.fit_note: The rule is about permission to scrape or train on data one can access, not about protecting personal data.

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to consult SMU's AI-specific guides" points instructors to institutional resources on integrity, research, teaching and workflow, which is faculty support (P63).
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to consult SMU's AI-specific guides on topics such as

units.why: "SMU is in the process of working with various departments on campus to gauge how AI can be best integrated in their curriculum" states an ongoing institutional effort to integrate AI in curricula; no type covers curricular integration planning, and it is not evidence collection (P55) or training (P70).
units.anchor: gauge how AI can be best integrated in their curriculum
units.uncovered_note: The university is working with departments to decide how AI can be integrated into their curricula.

units.why: The Q&A lists "students may become too reliant on Chat GPT and may not develop critical thinking skills" as a faculty worry; this explains the learning risk of reliance, P41, as rationale (informs).
units.anchor: students may become too reliant on Chat GPT and may not develop critical thinking skills

units.why: The answer names that "Chat GPT may reflect biases and stereotypes present in the data it was trained on", a statement of bias concern, P53.
units.anchor: Chat GPT may reflect biases and stereotypes present in the data it was trained on

units.why: "faculty may worry about the privacy implications of using Chat GPT" with the note that it "may collect and store data about students" is a fact-based privacy concern, P50.
units.anchor: faculty may worry about the privacy implications of using Chat GPT

units.why: "Design assignments that require students to apply what they have learned to real-world scenarios" recommends redesigning assignments so AI cannot easily complete them, P35.
units.anchor: Design assignments that require students to apply what they have learned to real-world scenarios

units.why: "Assignments that require students to draw on personal experience or conduct original research can also discourage reliance on Chat GPT" is an assignment-redesign suggestion, P35.
units.anchor: draw on personal experience or conduct original research can also discourage reliance on Chat GPT

units.why: "Use rubrics to clearly outline the expectations" with criteria on critical thinking and original thought changes grading criteria in response to AI, so P35.
units.anchor: include specific criteria related to critical thinking, analysis, and original thought

units.why: "Use plagiarism detection tools to check the authenticity of student work" recommends tools to identify AI-reliant work, P40; it does not caution about detector reliability.
units.anchor: Use plagiarism detection tools to check the authenticity of student work

units.why: "a sudden shift in writing quality or tone ... may indicate that a student has relied heavily on Chat GPT" names a kind of evidence to weigh, so P69; P40 does not fit because it is neither a tool nor a log.
units.anchor: sudden shift in writing quality or tone from one assignment to the next
units.fit_note: It treats a style shift as a possible indicator, not as sufficient proof.

units.why: "Chat GPT can be used to develop automated grading tools that can grade assignments, tests, or exams" says faculty may use AI for grading; it is instructor use of AI for teaching work (P59) rather than P46 because it permits rather than reserves grading for humans.
units.anchor: Chat GPT can be used to develop automated grading tools that can grade assignments, tests,
units.fit_note: It permits AI-built tools to do the grading itself, which touches P46 (human grading) in the opposite direction.

units.why: "Chat GPT can also be used to develop tools that can assist faculty in developing course curricula" is permitted faculty use of AI for course design, P59.
units.anchor: Chat GPT can also be used to develop tools that can assist faculty in developing

units.why: "Chat GPT can be used to develop communication tools that can help faculty communicate with students" is a permitted faculty AI use for course operations, P59.
units.anchor: develop communication tools that can help faculty communicate with students more effectively

units.why: "Faculty should use Chat GPT-generated content as a starting point and make necessary modifications" tells instructors how to treat AI drafts of emails and letters, P59 (should).
units.anchor: Faculty should use Chat GPT-generated content as a starting point and make necessary modifications

units.why: "it's important to ensure that the content is properly cited and attributed to the original source" is a citation duty for faculty-generated content; P59 is nearest as it concerns faculty AI use, though it is about citing sources.
units.anchor: it's important to ensure that the content is properly cited and attributed to the original
units.fit_note: It asks for citation of original sources in AI-generated text, not disclosure of the AI use.

units.why: "Faculty should be aware of the potential limitations of the tool and exercise their judgment" asks instructors to critically evaluate AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Faculty should be aware of the potential limitations of the tool and exercise their judgment

units.why: "ensure that they are using the tool in a manner that is consistent with academic integrity standards" binds faculty AI use to existing integrity rules, P77.
units.anchor: ensure that they are using the tool in a manner that is consistent with academic

units.why: "The Center for Teaching Excellence (CTE) has organized numerous workshops on AI and pedagogy", with one-on-one consultations offered, is CTE support for faculty learning AI, P63.
units.anchor: The Center for Teaching Excellence (CTE) has organized numerous workshops on AI and pedagogy.

units.why: "SMU will continue to review and consider more specific updated policies as this emerging field grows" says the guidance is provisional, P54.
units.anchor: SMU will continue to review and consider more specific updated policies as this emerging field

units.why: "all SMU community members should be aware of following existing best practices for data and privacy protections" directs everyone to follow existing data rules when using GPT tools, P77.
units.anchor: all SMU community members should be aware of following existing best practices for data and

units.why: "Publicly available generative AI systems are not secure or private!" is a warning that underpins the data rules, P50, informs.
units.anchor: Publicly available generative AI systems are not secure or private!

units.why: "Never submit any account information (usernames or passwords)" is a prohibition protecting confidential data in prompts, P50.
units.anchor: Never submit any account information (usernames or passwords)

units.why: "Never submit any Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or other sensitive or confidential material" protects personal data, P50.
units.anchor: Never submit any Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or other sensitive or confidential material

units.why: "Never submit queries or prompts that would lead to issues if they were to be made public" is a data-protection prohibition tied to the fact that public tools are not private, P50.
units.anchor: Never submit queries or prompts that would lead to issues if they were to be

units.why: "Never submit anything that includes your own or SMU's Intellectual Property (IP)" is an IP protection rule on inputs, P52 (ownership of AI inputs).
units.anchor: Never submit anything that includes your own or SMU's
units.fit_note: It restricts what IP may be entered into a tool, rather than who owns outputs.

units.why: "Always follow the relevant existing SMU policies on Data Protection, Acceptable Use, FERPA, Academic Integrity, Attribution and Ethics" ties AI use to existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: Always follow the relevant existing

units.why: "Never use public Generative AI tools to train AI models for people/human subjects unless those individuals have explicitly agreed" is a prohibition on a research data use, P62 (research and scholarship rules).
units.anchor: Never use public Generative AI tools to train AI models for people/human subjects
units.fit_note: It concerns human-subject data and consent, partly outside research and scholarship as such.

units.why: "This guidance is intended to include not just ChatGPT, but to all Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI chatbots" defines the scope of the guidance, P61.
units.anchor: This guidance is intended to include not just ChatGPT, but to all Large Language Models

units.why: "all queries/prompts made to an public AI engine are collected and retained by the organization providing the AI service" is a factual statement on retention, P50.
units.anchor: all queries/prompts made to an public AI engine are collected and retained by the organization

units.why: "AI models are designed to return responses that appear convincing, and all output should be viewed ... not as authoritative" warns users to doubt output, P31.
units.anchor: AI models are designed to return responses that appear convincing

units.why: "All output must be independently validated" is a binding verification duty, P31.
units.anchor: All output must be independently validated.

units.why: "the provenance of material and data reproduced by the models may be obscure, carrying the potential risk of copyright or other IP infringement" is a copyright risk statement, P52.
units.anchor: carrying the potential risk of copyright or other IP infringement

units.why: AI models "hosted by SMU researchers ... should be appropriately developed with SMU's IRB's policies" sets a research-governance rule deferring to the IRB, P62.
units.anchor: should be appropriately developed with SMU's IRB's policies

documents.title: Student Guidance (AI)
documents.summary: OIT's student guidance tells students to expect an AI statement in every course, to ask instructors when unsure and to treat AI like help from another person. A table maps Honor Code categories to AI violations and acceptable uses.
documents.stance_why: The guide says "Students should expect every course to include an explicit statement about the use or prohibition of Generative AI" and tells students to "discuss the parameters with their instructors", so the decision is left to courses and the document delegates; it sets only baseline limits such as no AI completing tasks.

units.why: "Students must familiarize themselves with the SMU Student Code of Conduct" binds students to the existing conduct code, P77.
units.anchor: Students must familiarize themselves with the SMU Student Code of Conduct

units.why: "students should review any School- or College-specific guidance" tells students to check school-level rules; nearest is P77 (follow existing university policy), but it points to lower-level AI guidance.
units.anchor: students should review any School- or College-specific guidance
units.fit_note: It sends students to school or college guidance, not only to university policy.

units.why: "Students should expect every course to include an explicit statement about the use or prohibition of Generative AI" tells students every course states its AI rule, P09.
units.anchor: Students should expect every course to include an explicit statement

units.why: "must respect the disciplinary and course-specific differences across the curriculum" says rules differ per course and students must follow each, P11.
units.anchor: must respect the disciplinary and course-specific differences across the curriculum

units.why: "students should discuss the parameters with their instructors as questions arise" is the ask-first guidance, P10.
units.anchor: students should discuss the parameters with their instructors as questions arise

units.why: "Students should treat the use of AI as they would assistance from another person" is the collaborator analogy under existing rules, P45.
units.anchor: Students should treat the use of AI as they would assistance from another person

units.why: "it is also unacceptable to have AI complete that task" bans having AI complete a task such as an essay, i.e. produce submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: it is also unacceptable to have AI complete that task

units.why: "Having access to data does not mean students have permission to scrape the data or use it to train an AI model" repeats the data-permission rule for students, P50.
units.anchor: Having access to data does not mean students have permission to scrape the data or
units.fit_note: The rule is about permission to scrape or train on data, not about personal data.

units.why: "it should never replace learning but serve as a partner" says AI must not replace the student's thinking or learning, P32.
units.anchor: it should never replace learning but serve as a partner

units.why: "open discussion about AI use is recommended" for values-based reasons asks for talk about AI rules, P66.
units.anchor: open discussion about AI use is recommended in these cases

units.why: Honor Code table: "Using ChatGPT or Copilot to write an entire essay when the instructor prohibits AI use" is labeled a violation of Cheating, so it classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Using ChatGPT or Copilot to write an entire essay when the instructor prohibits AI use.

units.why: "Entering quiz questions into an AI to get answers during an exam" is a violation example for exams, P22.
units.anchor: Entering quiz questions into an AI to get answers during an exam.

units.why: "Using AI for practice questions or self-testing before an exam (with no sharing of graded material)" is listed as acceptable, P14.
units.anchor: Using AI for practice questions or self-testing before an exam

units.why: "Asking AI to explain a concept, not to complete the graded task" is listed as acceptable, P12.
units.anchor: Asking AI to explain a concept, not to complete the graded task.

units.why: "Copying AI-generated text or images into a paper and not disclosing the use of AI" is a plagiarism example, so failing to disclose is the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Copying AI-generated text or images into a paper and not disclosing the use of AI.

units.why: "Submitting AI-generated code as original work" is named a plagiarism violation, P19 (AI must not produce what is submitted as one's own).
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated code as original work.

units.why: The acceptable example quoting AI output with attribution "Generated using ChatGPT, OpenAI, 2025." names tool, vendor and year, so P25.
units.anchor: Generated using ChatGPT, OpenAI, 2025.

units.why: "Using AI to summarize readings, but writing your own synthesis and citing accordingly" is listed acceptable, P14 (summaries as study aid).
units.anchor: Using AI to summarize readings, but writing your own synthesis and citing accordingly.
units.fit_note: Also requires own synthesis and citation.

units.why: "Using AI to generate fake survey results or lab data" is a fabrication violation: a general ban on fabricated data, P74.
units.anchor: Using AI to generate fake survey results or lab data.

units.why: "Letting AI hallucinate references and including them as if real" is a fabrication violation; P74 fits fabricated records, and the unit also implies verification.
units.anchor: Letting AI “hallucinate” references and including them as if real.
units.fit_note: Concerns unverified hallucinated references, close to P31.

units.why: "Using AI to simulate data for a methods course when explicitly permitted as a modeling exercise" is acceptable use of simulated data; no type covers permitted simulated data, and P74 bans fabrication so does not fit.
units.anchor: Using AI to simulate data for a methods course when explicitly permitted as a modeling
units.uncovered_note: AI may be used to simulate data in a methods course when the instructor explicitly permits it as a modeling exercise.

units.why: "Sharing an AI prompt that reproduces a current exam or assignment for others to submit" is a Facilitating Academic Dishonesty violation, P36.
units.anchor: Sharing an AI prompt that reproduces a current exam or assignment for others to submit.

units.why: "Running someone else’s assignment through AI to improve it for them" is a Facilitating Academic Dishonesty violation, P36.
units.anchor: Running someone else’s assignment through AI to improve it for them.

units.why: "Showing a peer how to properly disclose AI use or cite generated content" is acceptable; closest is P24 on disclosure but it concerns helping a peer.
units.anchor: Showing a peer how to properly disclose AI use or cite generated content.
units.fit_note: It permits helping another student disclose or cite, not the student's own disclosure.

units.why: "Deleting AI chat histories or falsifying screenshots to conceal unauthorized use" is an Impeding Investigation violation, P36.
units.anchor: Deleting AI chat histories or falsifying screenshots to conceal unauthorized use.

units.why: Claiming the AI wrote it by accident when evidence shows deliberate use is listed as an Impeding Investigation violation, P36.
units.anchor: when evidence shows deliberate use.

units.why: "Being transparent and cooperative about when and how AI was used if asked" is acceptable, a disclosure-is-safe style rule, P28.
units.anchor: Being transparent and cooperative about when and how AI was used if asked.
units.fit_note: It concerns cooperating with an inquiry, not penalties for disclosed use.

units.why: "Claiming AI-generated writing as your personal draft" is a Misrepresentation violation, P28 (nondisclosure as violation).
units.anchor: Claiming AI-generated writing as your personal draft.

units.why: "Uploading AI images or code to a portfolio without disclosure" is a Misrepresentation violation, P28.
units.anchor: Uploading AI images or code to a portfolio without disclosure.

units.why: The example reflection "AI assisted in outlining and grammar suggestions; final content authored by me." shows an acceptable disclosure statement, P24.
units.anchor: AI assisted in outlining and grammar suggestions; final content authored by me.

documents.title: Spring 2024: Syllabus Statement Options Regarding the Use of Generative AI
documents.summary: A Provost template gives instructors two ready syllabus statements for Spring 2024: one banning generative AI and one permitting it with attribution and responsibility for content. A write-in option lets faculty create their own.
documents.stance_why: The document is a menu titled "Syllabus Statement Options" with a ban statement, a "may be used with appropriate attribution" statement and a "Write-in Option", so per the codebook rule for templates the stance is delegates with the tiers listed.

units.why: The document title "Syllabus Statement Options Regarding the Use of Generative AI" and the "Write-in Option" show a menu of statements instructors may choose from, P05.
units.anchor: Syllabus Statement Options Regarding the Use of Generative AI
units.fit_note: Offers two ready statements plus a write-in, without color or level names.

units.why: "The use of any form of Generative AI is not permitted in this course" is the no-AI template, a default ban, P01.
units.anchor: The use of any form of Generative AI is not permitted in this course.

units.why: "assignments have been designed to ensure that you personally develop and demonstrate the knowledge and skills" gives the learning reason for the ban, P41.
units.anchor: The assignments have been designed to ensure that you personally develop

units.why: "you are encouraged to maintain clear evidence of your work (e.g., time-stamped drafts and notes...)" asks students to keep drafts and notes, P26.
units.anchor: encouraged to maintain clear evidence of your work
units.fit_note: Drafts are kept as evidence of ownership, not necessarily submitted.

units.why: "Any violation of these rules will be treated ... within the SMU Student Honor Code" classifies violations as honor-code matters, P36.
units.anchor: Any violation of these rules will be treated at the undergraduate level within

units.why: "an incident report will be submitted for review by the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards" states the escalation path when concern exists, P36.
units.anchor: will be submitted for review by the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards.
units.fit_note: It describes the procedural step (incident report) rather than the classification.

units.why: "Generative AI may be used with appropriate attribution" is the permit template, P02.
units.anchor: Generative AI may be used with appropriate attribution.

units.why: "In class, we will cover how Generative AI is used within this discipline" commits the instructor to teaching AI use, P44.
units.anchor: In class, we will cover how Generative AI is used within this discipline,
units.fit_note: Framed as the instructor teaching uses, abuses and attribution in class.

units.why: "Take responsibility for the content" makes the student answerable for what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: Take responsibility for the content

units.why: "AI can produce content that contains inaccurate information, offensive language/images, and biased or unethical representations" warns of flawed output behind the responsibility rule, P31.
units.anchor: AI can produce content that contains inaccurate information, offensive

units.why: "Provide clear attribution of your sources" is the attribution requirement of the permit template, P24.
units.anchor: Provide clear attribution of your sources.

units.why: "Any assignments that utilize Generative AI without attribution ... can be seen as potential academic dishonesty" makes failing to attribute the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Any assignments that utilize Generative AI without

units.why: "Faculty can choose to create a separate statement regarding AI use here" lets instructors write their own rule, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty can choose to create a separate statement regarding AI use here.

notes: Coder B. Only university-layer documents were included (no school or computing documents found). Many CTE page units come from a faculty Q&A and are advice rather than binding rules, so modality is should or informs.
